title: Sirach
subtitle: The wisdom of Jesus son of Sirach
lead: Sirach is a long book of wisdom written in Hebrew in Jerusalem by a teacher named Jesus son of Sirach, and translated into Greek by his grandson in Egypt.

audience.to: Young men studying with a Jerusalem teacher in the early 100s BC.
audience.why: To teach them to live by the fear of the Lord and the law of Moses.

lenses.name: Catholic
lenses.desc: The Catholic Church counts Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) among the deuterocanonical books of the Old Testament and reads it often in the liturgy.

lenses.name: Orthodox
lenses.desc: The Eastern Orthodox churches read Sirach in their Old Testament from the Septuagint, in the Greek order of chapters.

lenses.name: Protestant
lenses.desc: Protestants place Sirach among the Apocrypha: read for example of life by Anglicans and Lutherans, given no authority by Reformed churches.

lenses.name: Historical-critical
lenses.desc: Scholars read Sirach as the work of a Jerusalem scribe, Jesus son of Sirach, written in Hebrew in the early 100s BC and translated into Greek by his grandson in Egypt.

lenses.name: Jewish reception
lenses.desc: Sirach is not in the Jewish Bible, but the rabbis quoted it, and its Hebrew was copied by Jews into the Middle Ages, as the Cairo Genizah showed.

canon.summary: Sirach is in the Old Testament of Catholic and Orthodox Bibles. Protestant churches place it among the Apocrypha, and it is not in the Jewish Bible.
accepted_by: Read in the Septuagint Old Testament

provenance.b: A Jerusalem teacher, Jesus son of Sirach, wrote it in Hebrew; his grandson translated it into Greek.

rejected_why.b: The book is not among the books of the Hebrew Bible.

how_to_read.b: Read it as a teacher's collected instruction.
